response.rationale: The combination of GGCX compound heterozygous mutation, skin biopsy showing calcified elastic fibers, yellowish papules, progressive skin laxity, and factor X deficiency with prolonged PT strongly supports GGCX-related pseudoxanthoma elasticum with vitamin K-dependent clotting factor deficiency. Classic PXE (ABCC6) is less likely given the specific GGCX finding and coagulation abnormalities. Other differentials (cutis laxa, isolated factor X deficiency, EDS) fail to explain the full constellation of skin and coagulation findings.
